common_boundaries: A040/A041 values are raw bytes before firmware XOR and mask operations
P3/P5 values are external pin levels and are combined with MCU output latches by the MCU core
P6 is digital-only in the validated core; analog ADC values require another provider
cycle 4096 release timing is an explicit deterministic assumption
capture edges and ADC values are outside this board-I/O provider

scenarios.name: key-on
scenarios.proven_effect: A040.0 high exercises the 5ce5 wait loop; low releases to 5d0a
scenarios.assumption: the wait input changes once after key-on; no physical label or real delay is claimed

scenarios.name: crank
scenarios.proven_effect: P3.4 low can set BITS 5d when sampled in crank capture/scheduling routines
scenarios.assumption: the low window is a branch stimulus, not a claimed crank or cam waveform
scenarios.requires: external-3/CC0 capture events from a separate engine-position provider

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.proven_effect: after release, enabled input-mask bits 4 and 6 normalize high and select idle logical entry 3
scenarios.corroborated: logical entry 3 is the D/R A/C-off idle-target payload
scenarios.boundary: this does not prove raw pin polarity or create idle speed/load

scenarios.name: part-load
scenarios.boundary: part-load is selected from speed/load and calibration state, not a proven board-digital bit

scenarios.name: wot
scenarios.boundary: WOT tables are proven, but no A040/A041/P3/P5/P6 bit is proven to request WOT

scenarios.name: overrun
scenarios.boundary: overrun is speed/load/temperature qualified; these bytes deliberately do not invent a switch

scenarios.name: fault-inputs
scenarios.proven_effect: stuck A040.0 prevents startup release; low P3.4/P5.3/P5.4 and P6 rail values remain separately inspectable
scenarios.boundary: the combined byte pattern is not claimed to be one physical vehicle fault
